prompt: What does the passage call the master key to supernatural intelligence?

options.text: Inspiration
Meditation
Research
The fear of the Lord

explanation: 'Inspiration is the master key to supernatural intelligence.' The chapter is emphatic that it is inspiration, NOT mental exertion, that opens this world.

why.a: Correct. Inspiration is named the master key, and also the highest order of mental excellence's access route.
why.b: Wrong. Meditation is one of two ways to GENERATE inspiration, so it is a means to the key rather than the key.
why.c: Wrong. Research is one of the four ways to exercise the mind in Chapter 8.
why.d: Wrong. The fear of the Lord is the price of divine wisdom in Chapter 4, and is called its author and finisher there.

prompt: How does the author define inspiration?

options.text: The Spirit of God in motion in the mental faculty of a man
A sudden idea given by God to a willing heart
The witness of the Spirit to the spirit of a man
The illumination of scripture as it is read

explanation: 'I have defined inspiration as the Spirit of God in motion in the mental faculty of a man.' He compresses it further: inspiration, spirit in motion. A supernatural energizing of your mental faculty.

why.a: Correct. Motion is the key word, and the location is the MENTAL faculty specifically.
why.b: Wrong. Suddenness is not part of the definition, and the book gives methods for generating it.
why.c: Wrong. This locates it in the spirit, but the definition places it in the mental faculty.
why.d: Wrong. Scripture is said to have been DELIVERED by inspiration, which is a different claim.

prompt: Which scripture anchors the chapter on inspiration?

options.text: Job 32:8
2 Timothy 3:16
1 Corinthians 2:11

explanation: Job 32:8: 'But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding.' It is quoted three times in the book, and its Amplified rendering is given twice.

why.a: Correct. Job 32:8 is the anchor verse, returned to in Chapters 6, 7 and 10.
why.b: Wrong. Job 28:28 is the fear of the Lord being wisdom, used in Chapter 4.
why.c: Wrong. 2 Timothy 3:16 IS quoted in this chapter, but for scripture being GIVEN by inspiration, not as the anchor definition.
why.d: Wrong. 1 Corinthians 2:11 is also quoted here, introducing the definition, but Job 32:8 is the chapter's text.

prompt: What does the passage say Joseph knew how to do through inspiration?

options.text: Preserve food for fourteen years without the use of chemicals
Interpret every dream brought to him
Rear the colour of cattle he desired
Get a bountiful harvest without rain

explanation: Fourteen years without chemicals, cited to Genesis 41. Three examples run together in this passage and each belongs to a different man, so keep them apart.

why.a: Correct. Joseph and the fourteen years of food preservation.
why.b: Wrong. Dream interpretation belongs to Daniel in this book's examples, and is listed among what was found in him.
why.c: Wrong. That is JACOB, cited to Genesis 30:37-43, without a degree in veterinary medicine.
why.d: Wrong. That is ISAAC, cited to Genesis 26:1-12.

prompt: What is said of Jesus when He was to feed 5,000 people in a barren desert place?

options.text: "He himself knew what he would do"
He was moved with compassion toward them
He asked the disciples what they had
He lifted His eyes to heaven and gave thanks

explanation: John 6:6. It is quoted as evidence that inspiration supplies knowledge of what to do in advance, the same way Jacob knew the outcome of his cattle without trial and error.

why.a: Correct. This is the line quoted, and its force is foreknowledge of the method.
why.b: Wrong. A genuine gospel phrase from elsewhere that this book does not quote.
why.c: Wrong. Also genuinely in the account, also not the line used here.
why.d: Wrong. Also true of the episode, but not what the passage cites.

prompt: What is the author's position on the saying that genius is 99 per cent perspiration and 1 per cent inspiration?

options.text: He disagrees completely, because without that 1 per cent the 99 per cent equals zero
He agrees with it entirely
He reverses the figures to 99 per cent inspiration
He says the proportions vary from person to person

explanation: In Chapter 6 he says he disagrees completely, calling inspiration the covenant catalyst that makes the reaction take place at all. Note that in Chapter 8 he cites the same saying approvingly about studiousness, so the book uses it both ways.

why.a: Correct. Complete disagreement, on the ground that without the catalyst there is no reaction and everything else is zero.
why.b: Wrong here, though Chapter 8 does quote it without objection when arguing that the gift is not enough. This chapter states the disagreement explicitly.
why.c: Wrong. He does not restate the proportions; he argues the small share is decisive.
why.d: Wrong. No variation between people is proposed.

prompt: Who is quoted saying "Great men are not always wise: neither do the aged understand judgment"?

options.text: Elihu
Job
Solomon
David

explanation: Elihu, from Job 32:7-9. The point is that inspiration has nothing to do with a man's age, which is why Elihu, the youngest speaker, is the one who says it.

why.a: Correct. Elihu is named, and his speech contains the inspiration verse the chapter is built on.
why.b: Wrong. Job is the book, not the speaker of these verses.
why.c: Wrong. Solomon is quoted from Ecclesiastes and Proverbs, not from Job.
why.d: Wrong. David is quoted from Psalm 119 on meditation.

prompt: What two ways does the passage give for generating inspiration?

options.text: Singing and meditation
Prayer and fasting
Reading and reasoning
Quietness and separation

explanation: Two headings under HOW TO GENERATE INSPIRATION: SINGING and MEDITATION. Smith Wigglesworth's line introduces the section: 'If the Spirit does not move me, I'll move the Spirit.'

why.a: Correct. Singing and meditation are the two given.
why.b: Wrong. Prayer is one of four ways to EXERCISE the mind in Chapter 8, and fasting is never commended anywhere in this book.
why.c: Wrong. Reading and reasoning belong to Chapters 8 and 2 respectively.
why.d: Wrong, and it is a strong trap, because quietness and separation are two of the three factors of the right ATMOSPHERE in Chapter 7.

prompt: Who is quoted as saying "If the Spirit does not move me, I'll move the Spirit"?

options.text: Smith Wigglesworth
E. W. Kenyon
Kenneth E. Hagin
T. L. Osborn

explanation: Smith Wigglesworth, quoted to open the section on generating inspiration, since the whole point is that there is something you can do to get the Spirit moving.

why.a: Correct. Smith Wigglesworth is the name attached to this line.
why.b: Wrong. E. W. Kenyon said 'Make your brain work; it will sweat, but make it work', in Signposts On The Road to Success.
why.c: Wrong. Kenneth E. Hagin appears twice, once with the T. L. Osborn book on his table and once for the 1996 healing book.
why.d: Wrong. T. L. Osborn said 'When you stop learning, you start dying' and 'Every time you sin, something dies in you'.

prompt: Which prophet called for a minstrel, and what happened when the minstrel played?

options.text: Elisha, and the hand of the LORD came upon him
Elijah, and a still small voice came to him
Samuel, and the Spirit of the LORD fell on the company
Isaiah, and he saw the Lord high and lifted up

explanation: 2 Kings 3:15. Elisha needed divine inspiration to handle a pressing national issue, and music brought him into a supernatural depth of insight.

why.a: Correct. Elisha, the minstrel, and the hand of the LORD coming upon him.
why.b: Wrong, and it is the closest trap. Elijah and the still small voice are genuinely in this book, but in Chapter 7 under QUIETNESS, not here under singing.
why.c: Wrong. Samuel does not appear in this book.
why.d: Wrong. Isaiah is quoted often but that vision is not used.

prompt: What practical instruction does the passage give about singing?

options.text: To receive inspiration for the day, start singing as soon as you wake up in the morning
Sing only songs whose words are drawn from scripture
Sing aloud in company rather than alone
Sing before every important decision

explanation: Singing is described as working up the Spirit of God inside you, on the strength of Psalm 22:3, that God inhabits the praises of His people. So you can sing the Spirit of God into manifestation.

why.a: Correct. First thing in the morning, in order to receive inspiration for the day.
why.b: Wrong. No restriction on content is given.
why.c: Wrong. Company is not specified, and Chapter 7 actually commends solitude.
why.d: Wrong. Decisions are the product of REASONING in Chapter 2, and are not tied to singing.

prompt: What does the passage name as the enemies of inspiration?

options.text: Fear, anxiety and concerns
Noise, crowds and distraction
Pride, sin and comparison
Idleness, slothfulness and delay

explanation: Three enemies, and the mechanism is given: they weigh down your spirit so it chokes under their weight, and they paralyze your mental abilities.

why.a: Correct. Fear, anxiety and concerns are the three named.
why.b: Wrong. Noise and crowds are handled in Chapter 7 as things to escape through quietness and separation, which is a different list.
why.c: Wrong. Pride, sin and comparison are all obstacles in Chapters 5 and 9, but they are not the enemies of inspiration.
why.d: Wrong. Slothfulness and idleness come from the Ecclesiastes 10:18 epigraph in Chapter 2.

prompt: Why does the passage say the devil generates concerns, anxieties and burdens?

options.text: Because he knows he cannot handle you when you are inspired, so he keeps you too busy to open up to God's inspiration
Because he wants you to doubt your salvation
Because he cannot approach anyone who is at peace
Because worry is itself a form of sin

explanation: The motive is tactical. Inspiration makes you unmanageable to him, so he floods the mind with business to prevent it. It matches Chapter 9, where the devil is a mind-blocker.

why.a: Correct. He cannot handle an inspired man, so he crowds the mind instead.
why.b: Wrong. Assurance is never discussed in this book.
why.c: Wrong. This reverses the logic and is not stated.
why.d: Wrong. Worry is treated as a weight and a paralyser rather than as sin.

prompt: For what three things does the passage say you need grace?

options.text: To meditate effectively, to be studious, and to worship God into the realms of inspiration
To resist temptation, to forgive, and to endure hardship
To give, to serve, and to lead
To hear, to obey, and to wait

explanation: All the demands for enjoying inspiration require grace, and these three are the demands named. Genuine worship and praise that will stir up the Spirit inside you is said to require grace.

why.a: Correct. Meditation, studiousness and worship are the three, and each matches a practice taught elsewhere in the book.
why.b: Wrong. None of these three are raised in this connection.
why.c: Wrong. Giving belongs to Chapter 4 and is not part of this list.
why.d: Wrong. Willing and obedient is the Isaiah 1:19 condition from Chapter 2, not this list.

prompt: What does the passage say about people who read and read yet remain of average intelligence?

options.text: Nothing seems to be turning on inside them and everything still looks dark, because only the inspiration of the Almighty gives understanding
They are reading the wrong kind of books
They have not read enough to reach the threshold
They read for pleasure rather than for insight

explanation: Inspiration is the principal asset of every genius, and there is no substitute for it: your mental faculty will remain dormant without that breath of the Almighty from on high.

why.a: Correct. The missing ingredient is inspiration, not effort, which is this chapter's whole thesis.
why.b: Wrong. Choice of books is discussed in Chapter 2, but that is not the diagnosis here.
why.c: Wrong. Quantity is not the answer this chapter gives; that would be the perspiration view it rejects.
why.d: Wrong, and it is the closest trap, because 'many read for pleasure, no wonder they constantly live under pressure' IS in the book. It is in Chapter 8, under research.

prompt: How does the passage say God's wisdom was delivered to man in the Bible?

options.text: Via the channel of inspiration, not intellectualism
Through the careful research of its writers
By angels who dictated it to the prophets
Through the councils that assembled it

explanation: 2 Timothy 3:16 is quoted for it, and Luke 11:49 is added, where Jesus says 'Therefore also said the wisdom of God', which the author reads as referring to the Bible.

why.a: Correct. Inspiration rather than intellectualism is the contrast drawn.
why.b: Wrong. Research is a duty for the reader in Chapter 8, but it is not how the book says scripture came.
why.c: Wrong. Angels are never mentioned in this book.
why.d: Wrong. Canon formation is not discussed.

prompt: How does the passage explain the man whom the world calls fantastic?

options.text: He is an ordinary man with a fantastic Spirit moving on his inside, in his mental region
He has disciplined himself beyond what others are willing to attempt
He was born with unusual natural gifts
He has learned to imitate those who went before him

explanation: 'No, he's not fantastic, he only has a fantastic Spirit moving on his inside.' The credit is moved from the man to the Spirit in his mental region, which is exactly the definition of inspiration.

why.a: Correct. Ordinary man, fantastic Spirit, moving in the mental region.
why.b: Wrong. Discipline is the perspiration view this chapter argues against.
why.c: Wrong. Natural endowment is explicitly denied by calling him an ordinary man like anybody else.
why.d: Wrong. Standing on the shoulders of predecessors is Isaac Newton's line in Chapter 8, a different point.

prompt: What does the author say about the theories he has propounded in the Christian faith?

options.text: They are inventions with no physical products, but they have human products, men and women who authenticate them
They were gathered from many years of reading other authors
They were confirmed by councils of other ministers
They will only be understood after his lifetime

explanation: He says you will not find them in any book except the ones he wrote, and that the Spirit of God in motion inside his mental faculty gave birth to them.

why.a: Correct. Inventions without physical products but with human ones is the distinction he draws.
why.b: Wrong, and it is a genuine tension in the book, since Chapter 2 says he consults other authors on wisdom. Here he specifically says these came from no book.
why.c: Wrong. No confirmation process is mentioned.
why.d: Wrong. He points to living people as the present evidence.

prompt: How is meditation defined in this chapter?

options.text: Engaging a mental focus on an issue, for the purpose of enlightenment and illumination
Emptying the mind so the Spirit can fill it
Repeating a verse until it is committed to memory
Reading slowly and praying between each line

explanation: The definition is consistent across the book. Chapter 2 calls it the mental processing of knowledge into understanding, and Chapter 8 calls it giving mental focus to issues of interest with the aim of enlightenment and illumination.

why.a: Correct. Mental focus, aimed at enlightenment and illumination.
why.b: Wrong. Emptying is the opposite of the focus the book means, and it never appears.
why.c: Wrong. The author explicitly denies cramming, saying he eats scriptures rather than crams them.
why.d: Wrong. No such method is described.

prompt: Fill the blank: "Inspiration is the covenant {{1}} that makes the reaction take place at all."
explanation: Catalyst, borrowed from chemistry, which is why the sentence continues with reaction language: if the 1 per cent is not there, there is no reaction, and everything else is zero.

prompt: The passage teaches that mental exertion is the master key to a world of supernatural intelligence.

options.text: True
False

explanation: False. 'Inspiration, not mental exertion, is the master-key to a world of supernatural intelligence.' The book names exertion precisely in order to displace it.

why.true: Wrong. It picks the rejected half of a sentence built as a contrast.
why.false: Correct. Inspiration is the master key, and it is called your vital link with divine wisdom.

prompt: What does the passage say about genius and inspiration?

options.text: Without inspiration there is no genius, as ingenuity is a direct product of inspiration
Genius is rare, but inspiration is available to all
Genius may exist without inspiration but achieves little
Inspiration is given only to those already gifted

explanation: The claim is absolute. Chapter 6 later calls inspiration the principal asset of every genius, and says you cannot separate surpassing intelligence from inspiration.

why.a: Correct. No inspiration, no genius, because ingenuity is its direct product.
why.b: Wrong. Availability is not the claim being made in this sentence.
why.c: Wrong. This weakens an absolute statement into a relative one.
why.d: Wrong. Chapter 6 says inspiration has nothing to do with age, and treats it as accessible rather than reserved.
